309: (5) Some say that something baked or roasted, if one then cooks it in broth, there is a concern of cooking, and it is forbidden to place bread even in a kli sheni that is yad soledes bo. And some permit. {Rama: In a kli sheni. And some are lenient even in a kli rishon. And the custom is to be careful l'chatchila not to place bread even in a kli sheni as long as the hand is scalded in it.}
312: (6) 'If one cooked it afterward, etc.' — the Tur wrote this in the name of R' Eliezer Metz: even though there is no prohibition of cooking after cooking for a dry item, nevertheless there is cooking after roasting. His proof is from the chapter of kol sha'ah regarding a Passover offering — if one roasted it and then cooked it, one is liable. The Ravyah disagreed, and the Beit Yosef praised the Ravyah's challenge as strong.
314: (7) 'Even in a kli sheni' — the reason given in the Beit Yosef is that bread may easily cook even in a kli sheni. And those who permit hold like the Tur, that we do not find cooking in a kli sheni except for salt according to one opinion. See seif 9.
316: (8) 'And the custom is to be careful l'chatchila' — meaning that they do not place bread in the cholent broth, and it appears to me that those who slice onions very thin and place them in the broth should not place them while the hand is still scalded. And from what is written further in the gloss, the custom emerged to be careful even in a kli sheni, and b'dieved one should not forbid even in a kli rishon.
318: (17) 'Because of cooking' — even though there is no prohibition of cooking after cooking, there is cooking after roasting. And likewise there is roasting after cooking. Therefore it is forbidden to place something cooked near the fire without any vessel, for the heat would roast it.
320: (18) 'Even in a kli sheni' — for there are items that cook in it and we are not expert in all of them, and therefore for other items as well one should be stringent — see seif 9.
322: (19) 'Those who permit' — according to the view that a kli sheni does not cook, and from what was written in seif 4 in the name of Tosafos one should be stringent for it appears like cooking; but those who permit hold that according to the second answer in seif 9 there is no concern here.
324: (20) 'Even in a kli rishon' — since it is dry there is no cooking after baking.
326: (14) 'Cooking' — even though there is no prohibition of cooking after cooking for a fully cooked item, there is cooking after roasting. And likewise there is roasting after cooking.
328: (15) 'Even in a kli sheni' — the reason given in the Beit Yosef is that perhaps bread, because it softens easily, is cooked even in a kli sheni. And those who permit hold like the Tur, that we do not find cooking in a kli sheni except for salt according to one opinion.
330: (16) 'In a kli rishon' — since it is dry there is no cooking after baking.
332: (17) 'As long as the hand is scalded in it' — meaning that bread should not be put in the broth as long as the hand is scalded, and it appears to me that those who slice onions very thin and place them in the broth should not place them until after taking the pot off the fire.
334: (17) 'There is one who says' — like R' Yosi, Pesachim 41a, and likewise regarding Pesach where one roasted it, etc.
336: (18) 'Even in a kli sheni' — Shabbos 42b, and even according to the second version, because salt requires cooking, etc. But other items agree with the first version.
338: (19) 'And there is' — as written there 40b and the Magen Avraham, and according to the second version the first version is rejected.
340: (20) 'And some explain' — see Tosafos in Pesachim there s.v. Ula, etc. And we rule in Berachos there that boiled vegetables receive the blessing borei pri ha'adamah, and in Pesachim it is written that Ula holds that for blessings we require the taste of matza.
342: (4) 'Cooking' — see the Beer Heitev and see Noda B'Yehuda responsum: if there is nothing but water alone in a kli sheni, it is forbidden to place ground coffee into it since it changes its appearance.
344: (40) 'If it is cooked later in a liquid' — meaning that we placed it in a pot when it is being cooked with sauce. If we placed it in cold liquids, the problem would be cooking the liquids themselves.
346: (41) 'Because of cooking' — even though there is no prohibition of cooking after cooking for a dry item, there is cooking after roasting, even while still hot from the roasting [later authorities]. And likewise there is roasting after cooking.
348: (42) 'And it is forbidden to place bread, etc.' — he added another law here, and the reason for this opinion is that he holds there are items that cook even in a kli sheni because they are soft.
350: (43) 'Those who permit in a kli sheni' — he holds that a kli sheni does not cook anything.
352: (44) 'Even in a kli rishon' — he holds that the concept of cooking after baking or roasting does not apply, and the same in reverse.
354: (45) 'And the custom is to be careful, etc.' — meaning that they would not put bread into the cholent broth in the bowl which is a kli sheni, and all the more so one should be careful not to pour onto it from a kli rishon.
356: (46) 'L'chatchila, etc.' — and b'dieved even in a kli rishon one should not forbid, for there are those who are lenient.
358: (47) 'Even in a kli sheni' — regarding a kli shelishi, the Peri Megadim in the Eshel Avraham inclines toward leniency — see there.
360: (48) 'As long as the hand is scalded in it' — see the Chayei Adam who writes that where the hand is burned, all agree it cooks even in a kli sheni.
362: (37) 'Because of cooking' — we saw above the rule that there is no prohibition of cooking after cooking. The poskim disagree whether this rule applies only to cooking after cooking, or also to cooking after baking and roasting.
364: (38) 'When it is yad soledes bo' — according to the view that forbids cooking after baking, bread involves cooking. The Mechaber states that this is forbidden even in a kli sheni.
366: (39) 'And some permit — even in a kli rishon — for they are not concerned about cooking after baking. The Mechaber's view is that in this matter one may be lenient even in a kli rishon that is not on the fire.
368: (40) 'In a kli sheni' — according to this view there is cooking after baking and roasting; but specifically in a kli rishon, since a kli sheni does not cook even what has not previously been cooked.
370: (41) 'Even in a kli rishon — to place bread' — according to that view there is no cooking even after baking and roasting, and cooking bread is not rendering it fit to eat but only softening it.
372: (42) 'When it is yad soledes bo' — to take into account the view that although a kli sheni does not cook what is not cooked at all, it does cook what was baked or roasted.
375: 'Some say, etc., because of cooking' — see the Mishna Berurah — that there is also roasting after cooking; and see the Peri Megadim who cites Pesachim 41 that the first cooking was not annulled.
377: Summary of cooking after baking: the Shulchan Aruch is lenient in this matter, and the Rama agrees in principle, but the custom is to be stringent even in a kli sheni. And b'dieved if one placed bread even in a kli rishon that is not on the fire, one should not forbid it.
